source.title: Bilateral olfactory sensory input enhances chemotaxis behavior.

confidence_rationale: Direct behavioural demonstration that an olfactory signal functions as a near-raw spatial GRADIENT that can be followed for navigation -- a single functional olfactory neuron suffices for chemotaxis up a measured odour gradient, and bilateral input improves accuracy mainly by raising signal-to-noise. This is strong support for MECH-372's placement of smell at the LOW-adaptor-depth end: orientation behaviour (follow / approach / strengthen / weaken) is recoverable with minimal transformation of the raw chemical signal, in contrast to the multi-stage construction vision needs. Confidence held moderate because the model is Drosophila larva -- the gradient-primitive PRINCIPLE transfers but the specific biology is phylogenetically distant from REE's intended agent.
failure_signatures: Demonstrated in larval Drosophila with a single odour and an externally imposed monotonic gradient; it shows a near-raw gradient is SUFFICIENT for orientation, not that biological olfaction in general stays low-adaptor (mammalian odour-identity / mixture demixing may require substantial transformation, which would complicate MECH-372's 'smell = low-adaptor' as a blanket claim).

The bilateral-comparison benefit is largely an SNR effect, not a rich spatial-geometry computation -- so it supports 'gradient primitive' but offers no evidence for any structured olfactory MANIFOLD, leaving the depth of the olfactory adaptor under-specified at its upper bound.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Drosophila larvae perform chemotaxis up controlled, spectroscopically measured odour gradients; a single functional olfactory sensory neuron (unilateral input) provides sufficient information to navigate the gradient, and bilateral input enhances navigational accuracy chiefly by improving the signal-to-noise ratio of the concentration estimate.
mapping.ree_translation: Smell behaves as MECH-372 describes the low-adaptor end: a local gradient (stronger/weaker, nearer/farther) that can be followed, escaped, strengthened or weakened with a MINIMAL adaptor -- orientation falls out of the near-raw signal without a deep perceptual-manifold construction stage. This is the biological warrant for admitting a smell-like gradient sense as the earliest, cheapest V4 adaptor (PA-2) and for MECH-372's developmental-ordering corollary that gradient-like senses come first.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Larval-insect chemotaxis up an imposed gradient is far from REE's intended agent and from mammalian olfaction; it licenses 'a gradient can drive orientation with minimal transformation', not 'all olfaction is low-adaptor'. Odour IDENTITY/mixture perception (not tested here) may itself require a non-trivial adaptor, so the entry supports the gradient-PRIMITIVE reading of MECH-372 but not a strong claim that the whole modality is shallow.
mapping.source_context: Drosophila melanogaster larvae; high-resolution behavioural tracking in experimentally measured odorant gradients; unilateral vs bilateral olfactory neuron manipulations.

confidence_components.notes: source_quality high (Nat Neurosci, controlled measured gradients, clean genetics). mapping_fidelity good for the gradient-primitive reading. transfer_risk elevated (0.45): insect larva to a general low-adaptor principle is the main exposure, which is why overall confidence sits at 0.64 despite strong source quality.
